original.question_en: What was agreed on UCI multiplexing?
original.cypher: MATCH (a:Agreement)-[:MADE_AT]->(m:Meeting) WHERE a.content CONTAINS 'UCI' AND a.content CONTAINS 'multiplex' RETURN m.meetingNumber, a.resolutionId, a.content ORDER BY m.meetingNumberInt DESC LIMIT 10

seven_unit_review.assessment: The unchanged English asks what was agreed, with original a.content and preserved design/validation identifying substantive answer text. Confirming that some revision occurred is insufficient to identify its applicability. The exact removed if-condition changes conditional application into application without that qualification; preserving it unmarked changes the proposition. IDs or meeting names alone cannot answer this question.

Keep the original Agreement, MADE_AT and latest-meeting context. Both witnesses have their own explicit Agreement headers in the original #121 DOCX, immediately followed by confirmation of named #120bis working assumptions with revised text. The prior #120bis DOCX retains both conditions without strike. These are source-local amendments, not foreign quoted proposals.

The false-positive deferred Proposal has a separate retained-boundary repair route and cannot alone justify unsupported. Independently of that route, the two #121 own confirmation records are literal UCI/multiplex positives. No decision-only or normative-incorporation filter is added. Own Agreement source context identifies the revision target without assuming every formatting mark matters.

Decision records remain the counting unit. The original literal frontier has six above #121 and five tied at #121 with four slots: five legal identity choices, each including at least one witness. Excluding the separately deferred Proposal leaves five above plus all five at #121. No join multiplicity or arbitrary ID secondary order is introduced.

Direct frozen SQL reads confirm both own records retain the conditional words but no contentWithEquations/note/status property. I directly read all thirteen exported same-event full-property/incident-edge records and all fifteen broader alternative full-property records: other FFS removals target other bullets; the prior record preserves the old condition; none identifies deletion of this if-clause. This supports a bounded missing-source-status finding for the pinned representation, not a universal impossibility theorem.

The original meetingNumberInt DESC LIMIT10 has no secondary ID order. Actual preserved five tie alternatives were checked and cannot avoid both witnesses. The defect therefore is necessary for every original legal limited selection rather than a conveniently chosen tie. Tie ambiguity itself is not a clarification finding here.
